course_name_original: TRATTAMENTI SUPERFICIALI E RIVESTIMENTI PER MATERIALI METALLICI M (77883)
course_name_en: SURFACE TREATMENTS AND COATINGS FOR METALLIC MATERIALS M

learning_outcomes.text: Evaluate in which application it is necessary or convenient to modify the surface properties of materials in order to enhance corrosion and/or friction/wear resistance, or to develop specific chemical or physical properties.
Choose among the main surface modification and coating deposition technologies.

syllabus_topics: Basics on corrosion. Electrochemical (wet) corrosion: thermodynamic and kinetic aspects; protection methods. Chemical corrosion (high temperature oxidation): thermodynamic and kinetic aspects; protection methods. Coatings for corrosion protection.
Basics on friction and wear: Real surfaces; Contact between surfaces; Friction; Wear processes and mechanisms; Surface treatments and coatings for tribological applications.

Coatings deposited from vapor phase (PVD, CVD and PA-CVD processes): deposition technologies, properties and structures). Duplex treatments, nanostructured and adaptive (smart) coatings, carbon-based coatings. Thermochemical diffusion treatments (carburizing, nitriding, carbonitriding and nitrocarburising, sulfurising, boriding, aluminising, chromising and sherardising).

Coatings deposited from liquid phase: (i) Electroplating (chromium, nickel and zinc plating); Replacement of hard chromium coatings; Autocatalytic (electroless) deposition: Ni-P and Ni-B coatings, Ni-P matrix composite coatings. (ii) Conversion treatments (chromatising and alternative treatments; Phosphatising; Anodising; Plasma Electrolytic Oxidation)). (iii) Immersion in molten metal: hot-dip galvanizing, hot-dip aluminizing.
Coatings deposited from solid phase: thermal sprayed and welded coatings (hardfacing): deposition technologies, properties and structures. Cladding techniques.

Methods for the characterization of surface modified materials: morphology, roughness, composition, thickness, hardness, elastic modulus, adhesion, residual stress, fracture toughness, friction/wear and corrosion resistance.
Selection criteria for anti-friction/wear and anti-corrosion coatings and treatments are discussed throughout the whole course (with examples from case studies).
For each coating/surface treatment, the applicability to metallic materials as well as pros and cons are discussed.
teaching_methods: Lab practicals (focusing on characterization of coated/surface treated materials)
Optional seminars by experts from the industrial field
assessment_rules: The grade is expressed in /30. The minimum grade for passing the exam is 18/30, assigned if satisfactory knowledge of all subjects is assessed and there are no serious gaps. Working/athlete students may request an alternative exam date by contacting the Lecturer at least 14 days before the first scheduled exam date. Students with special teaching needs or disabilities should contact the Athenaeum office for adjustments, which must be submitted to the Lecturer 15 days in advance for approval.
